disciplines.name: Mathematics, statistics and computing
lead_departments: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada
committees: Standing Senate Committee on Banking, Commerce and the Economy
disciplines.evidence_culture: A reproducible method, published code and data, quantified uncertainty and a benchmark against a named alternative. What does not land: an accuracy figure with no baseline, a model with no deployment story, a claim about algorithmic risk with no measurement. Ottawa's digital and artificial intelligence files are crowded with vendors, so an independent, replicable number is the scarce thing you can supply.

best_stages.why: Departments draft digital, data and artificial intelligence options continuously and their analysts want a number they did not buy.
The standard, the audit method and the data collection instrument are all written at implementation, and almost nobody shows up for that.
Instruments governing data and automated decision-making reach Canada Gazette Part I, where a technical comment is published and citable.

disciplines.name: Physical and chemical sciences
lead_departments: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
committees: Standing Senate Committee on Energy, the Environment and Natural Resources
disciplines.evidence_culture: Measurement, method and detection limits. Regulatory chemistry lands when it speaks to a threshold, a substance list or a monitoring protocol. Peer-reviewed work carries weight, and a named uncertainty carries more. What does not land: hazard framing with no exposure estimate, and a call for more research with no decision attached to it.

best_stages.why: Substance assessments and thresholds appear in Canada Gazette Part I with a Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement you can challenge line by line.
Draft risk assessments and screening approaches are built inside departments long before a Gazette notice exists.
Monitoring protocols and laboratory methods become the operational rule once the regulation is in force.

disciplines.name: Earth and environmental sciences
committees: Standing Senate Committee on Energy, the Environment and Natural Resources
Standing Senate Committee on Fisheries and Oceans
disciplines.evidence_culture: Long time series, spatial coverage and a stated confidence interval. Federal environmental files run on monitoring data, so anyone holding a record that predates the department's own is immediately useful. What does not land: a single site presented as a national picture, and modelled projections with no observational anchor. Indigenous knowledge is expected alongside, not instead of, monitoring data.

best_stages.why: The Commissioner of the Environment and Sustainable Development audits on a published schedule, and anyone may file an environmental petition with a 120-day reply obligation.
Impact assessments and departmental science advice are assembled inside the department, where a data holder is welcome.
Gazette Part I windows on species listings, water and emissions instruments accept technical comment that is published and citable.

disciplines.name: Biological sciences
committees: Standing Senate Committee on Fisheries and Oceans
disciplines.evidence_culture: Population data, taxonomic authority and a defensible sampling design. Species at risk and biosecurity files run on assessments with named methods and reviewable data. What does not land: advocacy framed as science, and a conservation claim with no baseline. Where the work touches Indigenous territory, co-authorship and data governance under OCAP or CARE principles are read as a marker of quality.

best_stages.why: Species listings, permits and biosecurity instruments run through Canada Gazette Part I with a comment window tied to the science.
Status assessments and recovery strategies are drafted inside departments over months and analysts actively seek external data.
Recovery plans, monitoring designs and permit conditions are written at implementation and rarely revisited.

committees: Standing Senate Committee on Transport and Communications
disciplines.evidence_culture: Codes, standards and life-cycle cost. Federal infrastructure decisions are made against the National Building Code, National Research Council guidance and a cost per unit of service. What does not land: a demonstration project with no cost figure, and a resilience claim with no design load behind it. A number a Treasury Board analyst can put in a business case is the unit of influence.

best_stages.why: Program terms, eligibility rules and technical guidance decide what actually gets built, and they are written after the money is voted.
Infrastructure program design happens inside departments where a costed alternative is welcome.
Transport safety and building instruments reach Canada Gazette Part I, and the Building Canada Act joint committee reviews the exercise of major project powers.

committees: Standing Senate Committee on Transport and Communications
disciplines.evidence_culture: Test results, interoperability and spectrum or grid impact. disciplines.evidence_culture: Clinical evidence, device classification and a real-world safety record. Software as a medical device and artificial intelligence tools are the live files and the guidance on them is still being written.

disciplines.name: Medicine and health sciences
committees: Standing Senate Committee on Social Affairs, Science and Technology
disciplines.evidence_culture: Systematic reviews, trial evidence, population data and a cost-effectiveness figure. Health policy in Canada has a working evidence hierarchy and departments use it. What does not land: a single trial argued as a policy conclusion, and a recommendation that ignores that delivery is provincial. Jurisdiction is the first question every federal health analyst asks, so answer it before they do.

best_stages.why: Health Canada and PHAC draft options over months, both have a Departmental Science Advisor, and CIHR sets synthesis themes with departments.

disciplines.name: Agriculture, food and veterinary sciences
committees: Standing Senate Committee on Agriculture and Forestry
disciplines.evidence_culture: Field trial data, farm-level economics and traceable risk assessment. Agricultural policy is negotiated with producer organizations, so evidence that speaks to farm income and market access is read first. best_stages.why: Pesticide, feed, seed and food safety instruments run through Canada Gazette Part I and trade-affecting proposals carry at least a 70-day window.

Program terms and conditions decide which practices a farm can be paid to adopt.

disciplines.name: Psychology and cognitive sciences
committees: Standing Senate Committee on Social Affairs, Science and Technology
disciplines.evidence_culture: Effect sizes, replication and a named population. Behavioural evidence lands hardest when it names the intervention, the size of the effect and the group it applies to. What does not land: a laboratory finding presented as a service design, and a mental health recommendation that ignores provincial delivery. Departments increasingly run their own behavioural insight units, so an offer to test a design beats a call for awareness.

best_stages.why: Service design, forms, screening tools and delivery models are where behavioural evidence actually changes an outcome.
Departments buy behavioural research through CanadaBuys and set synthesis themes with the granting agencies.
Evaluations of social and health programs need outcome measurement that most departments cannot do in house.

disciplines.name: Economics and business
lead_departments: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
committees: Standing Senate Committee on National Finance
Standing Senate Committee on Banking, Commerce and the Economy
disciplines.evidence_culture: A costed number with a stated counterfactual. Finance and the Parliamentary Budget Officer both work in fiscal impact, incidence and elasticity, and a submission without a number is a submission about someone else's number. What does not land: a distributional claim with no data source, and a growth argument with no time horizon. Microdata access through Statistics Canada research data centres is a credential in itself.

best_stages.why: Two separate pre-budget processes run every cycle and a costed ask in the government's own vocabulary is exactly what they take.
The Parliamentary Budget Officer and departmental evaluation units both need independent estimates of what a program cost and delivered.
Finance and ISED draft options over months and buy economic analysis through CanadaBuys.

disciplines.name: Education

disciplines.evidence_culture: Outcome data across cohorts, and an honest answer on jurisdiction. Education is provincial, so federal traction comes through skills, student aid, official-language minority education, Indigenous education and immigration pathways. What does not land: a curriculum recommendation addressed to Ottawa, and an equity claim with no disaggregated data. Framing your finding as a labour market or a rights question is often what makes it federal.

best_stages.why: Eligibility rules, program terms and reporting requirements in federal transfers decide what provinces and institutions actually do.
Skills, student aid and official-language education programs are designed inside departments where synthesis work is welcome.
Transfer agreements and skills programs carry evaluation clauses on a published schedule.

disciplines.evidence_culture: Qualitative depth with a defensible sample, paired with a number a department already collects. Lived experience carries real weight in Canadian social policy, especially where a community holds the data. What does not land: a critique with no proposal attached, and research on a community done without it. Gender-based Analysis Plus is a mandatory step inside government, so evidence framed that way is directly usable.

best_stages.why: Social policy options are drafted over months with mandatory Gender-based Analysis Plus, and departments actively look for community evidence.
Eligibility rules, application forms and delivery models are where social policy either reaches people or does not.

disciplines.name: Law
lead_departments: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

committees: Standing Senate Committee on Legal and Constitutional Affairs
disciplines.evidence_culture: Doctrinal precision and comparative jurisdictions. A legal submission is read for whether the clause does what the department says it does, and whether it survives Charter and division-of-powers scrutiny. What does not land: a policy preference dressed as a legal conclusion. Drafted clause wording with a one-paragraph rationale is the highest-value object a law researcher can produce, and almost nobody supplies it.

best_stages.why: This is the only stage with formal submission channels, and a drafted amendment with a mover is the intervention that changes text.
Statutory review dates are written into the Acts themselves, so the calendar is public years ahead.
Legislative and regulatory teams draft the instrument long before it is public, and comparative analysis is welcome then.

disciplines.name: Political science and public administration

disciplines.evidence_culture: Institutional detail and comparative practice. Public administration research lands when it names the mechanism: the standing order, the directive, the reporting line, the incentive. Committees and the Library of Parliament both cite academic work on process directly, which is unusual and worth using.

best_stages.why: Public Accounts, the Auditor General and statutory reviews are structurally about how government works, which is the discipline's subject.

disciplines.evidence_culture: Archival authority, provenance and long-run context. Being cited by a Library of Parliament analyst is worth more than a submission nobody asked for.
